title: Multipath I/O Failover Events
exclusions: Limited to Linux Device Mapper Multipath events emitted by `multipathd`; it does not cover Windows MPIO, Solaris MPxIO, array-side port alarms, native NVMe multipathing, or generic kernel SCSI errors without a `multipathd` transition. A path failure means redundancy was reduced and traffic may have moved to another usable path; this log-only search does not prove that application I/O failed, that every path to a LUN was lost, or that a recovered path is currently healthy. Recovery-only messages are retained for dashboards but deliberately do not alert. Planned SAN tests are operational exceptions only when matched to an approved change; they are not silently suppressed by this UC.
evidence: When deployed, retain the dispatch/result artifact for saved search `linux_multipath_path_failure_events`, the matching raw `multipathd` records (including `_time`, `host`, `source`, path and map where present), and an incident-time `multipathd show paths raw format "%d|%m|%t|%T|%o|%w"` snapshot. Link approved maintenance tickets to suppressed alerts. This catalog entry neither creates an `audit_evidence` index nor claims that those artifacts already exist.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a non-production test index configured as the search's `index`, ingest a `sourcetype=syslog` event such as `Jul 28 09:00:00 san-test-01 multipathd[1234]: checker failed path 8:16 in map mpatha`. Run the search over that time and verify one row with `host=san-test-01`, `path=8:16`, `multipath_map=mpatha`, `event_state=failed`, `event_count=1`, and `severity=high`. Separately, an approved lab invocation of `multipathd fail path <test-path>` may be used only when the storage owner confirms redundant paths and rollback.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest `san-test-01 multipathd[1234]: sdb: reinstated` and an unrelated application event containing `path failed`. The recovery-only event must be classified before the final filter but produce no alert row, and the unrelated event must fail the daemon/signature scope. Also verify that a `multipathd` informational line with none of the enumerated transition signatures produces no row. Do not disconnect a production SAN path to perform this test.

dataSources: Linux `multipathd` service messages written by journald/rsyslog to `/var/log/messages`, `/var/log/syslog`, or `/var/log/daemon.log`, monitored by a Universal Forwarder into `index=os` with `sourcetype=syslog`. Monitor exactly the local plaintext destination that contains the daemon records; journal-only hosts must first route/export the unit's records to a supported text or syslog input.
app: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase 833) on a Universal Forwarder for Linux log collection; no custom multipath add-on is required.
spl:
index=os sourcetype=syslog earliest=-10m@m latest=@m ("checker failed path" OR "reports path is down" OR "unusable path" OR "path offline" OR "no access to this device" OR "reinstate failed" OR "reinstated" OR "reports path is up")
| eval daemon=coalesce(process, appname, program)
| where daemon="multipathd" OR match(_raw, "(?i)\bmultipathd(?:\[\d+\])?:")
| dedup host _time _raw
| rex field=_raw "(?i)checker failed path\s+(?<path>\S+)\s+in map\s+(?<multipath_map>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "(?i)multipathd(?:\[\d+\])?:\s+(?<multipath_map_from_checker>[^:\s]+):\s+(?<path_from_checker>[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)\s+-\s+\S+\s+checker reports path is"
| rex field=_raw "(?i)multipathd(?:\[\d+\])?:\s+(?<path_from_prefix>(?:\d+:\d+|[^:\s]+)):\s+"
| eval path=coalesce(path, path_from_checker, path_from_prefix, "unknown"), multipath_map=coalesce(multipath_map, multipath_map_from_checker, "unknown")
| eval event_state=case(match(_raw, "(?i)reinstate failed"), "reinstate_failed", match(_raw, "(?i)checker failed path|reports path is down|unusable path|path offline|no access to this device"), "failed", match(_raw, "(?i)reinstated|reports path is up"), "recovered", true(), "other")
| where event_state IN ("failed", "reinstate_failed")
| stats count as event_count earliest(_time) as first_seen latest(_time) as last_seen values(source) as sources values(_raw) as sample_events by host path multipath_map event_state
| eval duration_minutes=round((last_seen-first_seen)/60, 1), severity=if(event_state="reinstate_failed" OR event_count>=3, "critical", "high")
| sort 0 - last_seen
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
description: Detects Linux Device Mapper Multipath path-checker failures, unusable paths, and failed reinstatement attempts from `multipathd` syslog records. It extracts the path and multipath map when the daemon supplies them, preserves unknown values rather than inventing identifiers, and distinguishes failure from recovery signatures across common multipath-tools versions.
value: Detecting the first failed multipath path helps Linux and storage teams prevent a later path loss from turning degraded redundancy into an outage. Preserved map, path, host, state, and message context improves investigation of HBA, fabric, target-port, configuration, and path-flapping problems even while I/O still succeeds.
implementation: Forward the plaintext system log that receives `multipathd` unit messages as `sourcetype=syslog`, schedule the search every five minutes over a closed ten-minute window, and alert when it returns any row. Treat one failure as high priority and a failed reinstatement or three matching events in the window as critical; these are operational defaults, not vendor-prescribed thresholds. Verify current topology with `multipathd show paths` before changing storage.
visualization: Alert table with host, path, multipath map, state, count, first/last seen, severity, and sample event; 24-hour timeline split by event state; single values for affected hosts and failed reinstatements. Use a separate recovery panel that omits the alerting filter.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Approved fabric failover test** — A SAN, HBA, cable, or target-port test deliberately moves traffic. Correlate the exact host, path, map, and event time with the approved change before suppressing it.

2. **Operator-issued multipathd command** — `multipathd fail path` creates a real transition during controlled maintenance. Confirm the terminal or automation record and retain the failure as test evidence.

3. **Duplicate syslog ingestion** — Overlapping file monitors or a forwarding loop can replay one daemon message. Compare `_raw`, host, source, and original timestamp; fix collection instead of widening the threshold.

4. **Synthetic control event** — A test record can enter a production index without a marker. Require test events to carry a dedicated host or index and remove them from operational alert routing.

**Suppression mechanism:** use a time-bound exception lookup keyed by `host`, `path`, and `map`, with change ID, owner, start, and expiry. Repeated down/up changes, `reinstate failed`, or checker errors are not false positives merely because another path still carries I/O.
mitreAttack: N/A (Operational storage-path availability monitoring; no security technique is asserted.)
detailedImplementation:
Step 1 — Prerequisites and scope

Enable Device Mapper Multipath on each in-scope Linux host and confirm `systemctl is-active multipathd` returns `active`. The Linux/storage operator needs permission to read the service journal and issue read-only `multipathd show` commands; the Splunk administrator needs permission to deploy a Universal Forwarder input, route events to `index=os`, create a scheduled search, and configure alert actions. Install the Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux on the forwarder. No premium Splunk product or CIM acceleration is required. Before alerting, record the host's normal map/path inventory with `multipathd show paths raw format "%d|%m|%t|%T|%o|%w"`: `%d` is the path device, `%m` its map, `%t` the device-mapper state, `%T` the checker state, `%o` the online state, and `%w` the WWID. Device Mapper `active` is not the same field as checker `ready`; Red Hat documents `ready` and `ghost` as usable and `faulty`, `shaky`, timeout, removed, wild, unchecked, or delayed conditions as unavailable or not reinstated. This UC alerts from transitions in logs and uses the command only as the current-state corroboration point.

Step 2 — Configure and verify collection

First find the one plaintext file receiving `multipathd` records: compare `journalctl -u multipathd --since '-15 min'` with `/var/log/messages` (commonly RHEL-family), `/var/log/syslog`, or `/var/log/daemon.log` (distribution dependent). On a journal-only host, configure the site's supported journald-to-rsyslog/syslog route or another approved text export; a Universal Forwarder file monitor cannot read the binary journal directly. Do not monitor two files containing the same messages. In `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_nix/local/inputs.conf`, deploy only the applicable stanza, for example:

```ini
[monitor:///var/log/messages]
disabled = 0
index = os
sourcetype = syslog
```

Restart the forwarder after changing `inputs.conf`. Confirm coverage with `index=os sourcetype=syslog earliest=-15m (process=multipathd OR appname=multipathd OR program=multipathd OR "multipathd[") | stats count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(source) as source by host`. Event volume should normally be low and transition-driven. If no recent event exists, compare a harmless service status/journal check; do not manufacture a path failure in production. If events are present in the file but absent from Splunk, check forwarder read permission, input precedence with `splunk btool inputs list --debug`, forwarding connectivity, and whether `index=os` exists and is searchable by the alert owner.

Step 3 — Create the search and understand its states

Save the documented SPL as `linux_multipath_path_failure_events`. Run every five minutes with the closed window `earliest=-10m@m latest=@m`; the overlap tolerates forwarding delay, so configure result throttling on `host,path,multipath_map,event_state` for 15 minutes to avoid duplicate pages. The base search uses parenthesized, known multipath-tools message fragments and then requires either a parsed daemon field or a raw syslog `multipathd[pid]:` prefix. This prevents an unrelated application's words from entering the result. The first `rex` handles upstream `checker failed path <major:minor> in map <alias>` records. The second handles current map-prefixed checker output such as `<map-or-WWID>: <device> - tur checker reports path is down`; the third handles older `<device>:` and `<major:minor>:` prefixes. Missing map/path values remain literal `unknown` because not every multipath-tools release includes both identifiers in every message.

`event_state=failed` covers checker-down, checker-failed, offline, disconnected/no-access, and unusable-path transitions. `event_state=reinstate_failed` means multipathd attempted to return a path to service but could not. `event_state=recovered` covers `reinstated` or checker-up signatures and is intentionally removed by the alert filter; remove that filter only for the recovery timeline. One failed/unusable transition is a high-priority result because redundancy has changed. A failed reinstatement, or three matching records for the same host/path/map/state in ten minutes, is marked critical as a local flapping/escalation default. These thresholds are not supplied by multipath-tools and must be reconciled with path count, array design, polling interval, and on-call policy. The search does not claim all paths are down.

Step 4 — Validate safely

Use the positive and negative `controlTest` records in a non-production index (temporarily substitute that index in a copy of the saved search). Verify the positive record extracts `8:16` and `mpatha`; verify recovery-only and unrelated records return no alert rows. Also test a current-format record such as `multipathd[1234]: 3600testwwid: sdb - tur checker reports path is down` and require `multipath_map=3600testwwid`, `path=sdb`, and `event_state=failed`. Compare Splunk `_time` and `_raw` byte-for-byte with `journalctl -u multipathd` or the monitored file to detect timestamp errors, truncation, and duplicate ingestion. Confirm in the multipathd console (opened with `multipathd -k`) that the same path, map, device-mapper state, checker state, and online state agree with the Splunk result. With storage-owner approval on a redundant lab map, capture topology before and after `multipathd fail path <path>`, then reinstate the path and confirm both the failed and recovery records exist; do not use cable removal as a routine control test. After any test, require `multipathd show paths` to show the expected device-mapper, checker, and online states. A passing log test proves collection and search behavior, not end-to-end application I/O continuity.

Step 5 — Operationalize, evidence, and troubleshoot

Route high results to Linux/storage operations with host, path, map, first/last seen, count, source, and raw sample. Route critical results to the storage incident path. The responder should immediately run the formatted `multipathd show paths` command, inspect `multipath -ll`, identify the WWID/map and remaining usable paths, correlate array and fabric alarms, and check the approved change calendar. Never reinstate a path solely to clear an alert; repair or validate the transport and follow the storage vendor's recovery procedure. Preserve the saved-search dispatch, raw records, command snapshot, incident identifier, and any maintenance approval as evidence.

If no `multipathd` events arrive while the monitored file contains them, inspect the forwarder input, file permissions, and routing queue before trusting the alert. If `path` or `multipath_map` is `unknown`, inspect the raw distribution-specific message before extending the extraction; do not infer a LUN from the host alone. If only recovery events appear, collection is working and the alert correctly stays quiet. If events duplicate, look for two monitored files, rsyslog forwarding loops, or index-time cloning. If logs report repeated down/up transitions, do not suppress them as noise: review the configured `polling_interval`, checker choice, and the `log_checker_err`/shaky-path controls with the storage owner. If the live command shows `failed`, `faulty`, `shaky`, `i/o timeout`, `delayed`, `offline`, or `dead` while no event was indexed, treat that as collection incompleteness and repair the source path before relying on this UC.
grandmaExplanation: We warn when a server loses one of its routes to shared storage, giving the team time to fix the remaining safety net before another route fails and causes an outage.
